card: Adds functional test coverage verifying that during Initial Block Download, outbound full-relay and block-relay-only peers are disconnected when their headers chains do not meet nMinimumChainWork, while inbound and manual peers remain connected. This node eviction behavior was previously untested because functional tests typically use manual connections and default to zero minimum chain work. No dependencies are stated.
changed_since_previous: The full patch is now provided; the implementation matches the previous description.
evidence: PR description: 'While in IBD, outbound peers (full-relay and block-relay-only) whose headers chain has less work than nMinimumChainWork are disconnected. This behavior was not covered by any test...'
problem: Bitcoin Core's peer disconnection logic for outbound peers serving chains with insufficient work during IBD was not covered by the functional test suite, because functional tests default to zero minimum chain work and typically connect nodes via manual connections.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause a functional test failure or flake and cannot affect node behavior.

summary: Adds a test case to `feature_minchainwork.py` verifying that during Initial Block Download, outbound full-relay and block-relay-only peers serving headers chains below `nMinimumChainWork` are disconnected. It also checks that inbound and manual peers serving the same insufficient-work headers remain connected.
